description:
FILED s473t1 (Opus, the 13-file early-stop triage).  Same family as the
already-fixed `skip_without_dynamic_extension` (cl/pcl-test.lisp carries the
note: "PCL used to skip unconditionally -- a claim about the environment it
never checked").

    # perl-tests/t/test.pl
    sub is_miniperl { return 0; }
    sub skip_if_miniperl { my ($reason,$n) = @_; skip($reason, $n // 1); }

    # perl's own t/test.pl
    sub skip_if_miniperl { skip(@_) if is_miniperl(); }

The two PCL subs contradict each other, and the comment above the second
("PCL can't run subprocess tests with -C/-CE switches") is about a different
helper's callers.

CALL SITES: 15 in 9 files -- magic.t 5, ref.t 2, split.t 2, do.t, eval.t,
method.t, closure.t, warn.t, signatures.t 1 each.

MEASURED (--jobs 1, s473t1 tree, with the body changed to perl's `if
is_miniperl()` and reverted afterwards) -- pass/fail/skip/ran:

    file        before                   after                    verdict
    magic.t     158/31/16  ran 205       163/37/6   ran 206       +5 pass  GOOD
    ref.t       196/15/31  ran 242       199/15/25  ran 239       +3 pass, -3 rows
    method.t    76/22/26   ran 124       77/22/0    ran  99       -25 rows  BAD
    eval.t / do.t / closure.t / warn.t / split.t   unchanged

method.t is the reason this is not a one-line change: its 26-row SKIP block
(`skip_if_miniperl('file handles as methods requires loading IO::File', 26)`)
CRASHES its top-level form when it actually runs, so un-skipping it costs the
file 25 produced rows.  Do it per call site, with the rows read, like the
s464ay kvhslice/splice restoration -- not in one edit.

It is a harness change: the full sweep is owed, and both baselines are edited
ROW BY ROW.
subject: perl-tests/t/test.pl's `skip_if_miniperl` skips UNCONDITIONALLY while its own `is_miniperl` returns 0 -- 15 call sites in 9 files manufacture skips; making it honest is +8 passing rows in two files and -25 produced rows in method.t
